Cross-refer: The administrative enforcement scheme is discussed in greater detail at ¶ 7:1031 ff., 7:1050 ff. • [3:672.1] Neither the employee's filing of a discrimination charge, nor the subsequent DFEH investigation, conciliation or issuance of a “right to sue” letter would appear to constitute a “claim” because they do not result in a binding adjudication of liability or an award of damages. • [3:672.2] In contrast, the filing of a civil action by the DFEH (a “judicial proceeding”) would satisfy the definition of “claim” for purposes of determining insurance coverage. [See Gov.C. § 12965(a)] [3:673 - 3:674] Reserved. (2) [3:675] Absent policy definition: Where the policy does not define “claim,” the common law definition will control: i.e., a “claim” is a demand for something as a right or as due, as opposed to a mere inquiry requesting an explanation, or a mere expression of dissatisfaction.
